title: Rollout orchestration parity for canary/A-B/shadow across Hosted, Dedicated, Private
creator: Marcus Li
description: Implement a unified rollout orchestration layer that supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, shadow traffic, and auto-rollback with consistent configuration semantics across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.
background: Teams frequently configure ad-hoc canaries and A/B experiments with different tooling for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. This causes operational drift, brittle rollouts (especially when moving customers between modes), and gaps in telemetry and rollback behavior in Private installs where external services are limited.
goals: Provide a single declarative rollout spec that maps to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private runtimes
Support canary traffic weights, time-based ramps, and deterministic A/B allocations
Enable shadow traffic for offline validation without affecting user-facing latency or cost accounting
Implement auto-rollback policies driven by platform signals (errors, latency regressions, eval metric drift)
Preserve security and compliance constraints for Private (no external telemetry egress unless configured)
Ensure parity in user-visible behavior and UX in Console and API across deployment modes
acceptance_criteria: A single rollout config schema (yaml/json) accepted by Redwood API and Console that validates for all three deployment modes
Canary rollout: ability to route N% of production traffic to new model variant with staged ramp (e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) and manual/auto advance
A/B test: stable allocation buckets (A/B/C) with independent scoring and metric aggregation
Shadow traffic: send a copy of 100% of live requests to a candidate model without counting responses toward production latency SLOs or billing by default
Auto-rollback: configurable policy that will revert routing within <2m of detecting a P0 threshold breach (error spike, 99th latency increase > X, drop in quality score)
Behavioral parity checks: Console shows identical rollout state and traffic weights for Hosted/Dedicated; Private shows same semantics but indicates any constrained features
End-to-end e2e test harness that simulates ramp, fault injection, and auto-rollback for each deployment mode
proposed_solution: Introduce a rollout orchestration service that accepts a canonical 'rollout_spec' object. The service emits platform-specific routing commands: Hosted uses internal router and weights; Dedicated updates pool routing rules and autoscaler hints; Private generates a local controller manifest and an optional operator that runs inside the customer's control plane. Shadow traffic is implemented by fanout in the serving runtime; where fanout cannot be performed due to network constraints, we fall back to log-based replay.
config_constraints: Private deployments may not allow outbound connections to our telemetry ingestion endpoints; rollout controller must support local telemetry buffering and operator-controlled opt-in
Dedicated clusters may have fixed GPU pools preventing instant elastic scaling; rollout plans must include throughput reservation hints
Hosted supports fine-grained weight changes with sub-second cutover; Dedicated/Private may require longer propagation windows (30s-5m)
Secret management differences: KMS/HSM integration in Private alters how rollout controller fetches model keys
Network policies in Private can restrict fanout; in those cases shadowing must be a local sidecar copy or asynchronous replay
rollout_matrix: Hosted: supports percent canary, instant traffic split, remote auto-rollback via control plane, full telemetry (fast)
Dedicated: supports percent canary via pool routing, slower propagation, autoscaler hints, partial telemetry depending on retention tier

Private: supports canary if operator installed; otherwise recommend blue/green with DNS-based switch. Shadowing supported if sidecar enabled; otherwise use log replay. Auto-rollback implemented as operator-managed manifest revert
rollback_conditions: Production error rate increase > 3x baseline for 5m
99th percentile latency increase > 200ms relative to baseline for 10m
Automated eval set metric drop (e.g., Rouge/BLEU/embedding-similarity) beyond configured delta
Customer error reports flagged from support dashboard (manual trigger)
Data drift detector raises high-severity alert
monitoring_signals: latency_p50/p95/p99: broken down by model variant and backend
quality_score: synthesized from evaluation prompts and online feedback
shadow_discrepancy_rate: semantic divergence between primary and shadow responses
testing_plan: Unit tests: rollout_spec validation and platform translator
Integration: end-to-end harness that runs canary ramps with synthetic traffic and fault injection (hosted/dedicated/private operator)
Staging dry-run: deploy to staging tenants and run shadow traffic to measure divergence and edge cases
Chaos tests: simulate network partitions, operator downtime, and delayed telemetry
Security review: ensure Private operator does not exfiltrate secrets and respects egress policy
migration_steps: Add rollout_spec v1 to API with opt-in flag for existing customers
Ship Console UX for creating and visualizing rollout specs
Deploy translator for Hosted first (fast feedback), then Dedicated, then Private operator
Run pilot with 3 internal teams and 2 enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private
Iterate on auto-rollback thresholds and default signals based on pilot telemetry
implementation_notes: Reuse existing routing & model-variant metadata in runtime to minimize code churn
Leverage current KV cache tagging to attribute traffic per-variant for cost accounting
Add 'shadow' flag to runtime request path that enables non-blocking fanout and captures responses for offline comparison
Operator for Private should be packaged as a small control-plane sidecar with explicit opt-in for telemetry egress
risks: Private customers with strict egress policies may not be able to support real-time auto-rollback without on-prem operator — increases time-to-revert
Incorrectly calibrated auto-rollback thresholds could cause false positives and unnecessary rollbacks
Performance impact of shadow fanout on serving latency if not implemented as asynchronous background tasks
Operational complexity in surfacing consistent UX across modes could confuse SREs
notes: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting; agreed canonical rollout_spec schema and that Hosted will be first integration
